note:
[b]Good jobs[/b]

[b]How do we measure this?[/b]
Percentage of employees in NI (aged 16-64) in good jobs. For the purposes of this metric a ‘good job’ is one which meets the following requirements: a permanent contract; and a non zero-hour contract; and earning the Real Living Wage (RLW) or more.

[b]Source[/b]
Good Jobs in Northern Ireland, NISRA
[url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/publications/good-jobs-northern-ireland]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/publications/good-jobs-northern-ireland[/url] 

[b]Impact of Covid-19[/b]
Users should note that the Coronavirus Job Retention Scheme (CJRS) was in place in 2020 and 2021. The CJRS was a temporary scheme providing grants to employers to pay 80% of staff wages and employment costs up to a cap per person per month designed to help employers whose operations were affected by coronavirus to retain their employees. 16% of all employees in the NI survey in 2020 and 7% in 2021 were identified as being furloughed with reduced earnings.

[b]Further information[/b]
1. The data for this indicator is collected from the Annual Survey of Hours and Earnings (ASHE) as it captures information on all three ‘good jobs’ criteria. 
2. The results relate to employees in the working age population (aged 16 to 64).
3. The reference date for the latest survey was 30th April 2025.
4. Over the pandemic period, earnings estimates were affected by changes in the composition of the workforce and the impact of the CJRS, making interpretation difficult. In particular, the 2020 and 2021 data are subject to more uncertainty and should be treated with caution. Furthermore, 2022 annual earnings, which relate to the 2021/22 financial year, were affected during the first six months of the year. Therefore, over these periods users are encouraged to focus on long-term trends rather than year on year changes.
5. Further information on ASHE can be obtained from the ASHE 2025 publication at the following link: [url=https://www.nisra.gov.uk/publications/employee-earnings-ni-2025]https://www.nisra.gov.uk/publications/employee-earnings-ni-2025[/url]
